summary: Complete target-level continuation of the accepted Z.3 packet’s 25 Z.6 targets: eight comparison/coherence refinements, exact support/descent supplier routing, discriminating degree-zero tests and a compact native suggested file. No second K₀, Cartan map, geometric determinant, support category or projective-bundle theorem is planned. Coverage is planned, with inherited enriched-coherence and arbitrary-regular approximation requests explicit.

nodes.title: Naturality of the affine degree-zero comparison diagram
nodes.statement: Write c_A for the existing comparison RingK0(A) ≅ ExactK0(P(A)) ≅ π₀K(P(A)). For every unital ring map f:A→B, c_B ∘ RingK0.map(f) = π₀K(B⊗_A−) ∘ c_A. For commutative A the affine sheafification comparison and E↦E[0] identify this SAME map with K₀(Vect(Spec A))→π₀K(Perf(Spec A)); the diagram remains commutative after base change. On commutative rings all comparisons preserve tensor products and units. The noncommutative version uses perfect module complexes, without invoking Spec A.
hypotheses: P(A) is the essentially small exact category of finite projective left A-modules with its induced split exact structure. Fix universe/small-model transports as in K.1.
The scheme comparison is asserted only for commutative unital rings. No flatness of f is needed on projectives: their exact sequences split.
proofSteps: Use the old Z.1 equivalence with ExactK0 and K.1’s loop-class normalisation. Both composites on [P] give the loop class of B⊗_A P; ExactK0.hom_ext proves equality.
For commutative A use S.2/affine-k-theory-comparison and the finite-projective/sheaf equivalence imported by Z.5. The object P sheafifies to P~ and both routes give P~[0].

Check tensor comparison on pairs of projective classes using the imported biexact pairing, and the unit on [A]. For general rings use K.4/gillet-waldhausen and Weibel V.2.7.2, not S.2’s scheme-only affine statement.
acceptance: The zero ring has zero K₀; no integer-rank isomorphism is claimed for it.
For a field extension F→E, the resulting ℤ→ℤ map is the identity, not multiplication by [E:F].
For F×F→F the first projection sends the two idempotent projectives to F and 0.

sources.locator: II.2, book pp.68–69 (PDF pp.76–77); IV Proposition 6.2, book p.319 (PDF p.327); IV Corollary 7.2, book p.328 (PDF p.336); V.2.7.2, book p.383 (PDF p.391)
sources.match: These locators give scalar extension, the object-class loop, the plus/Q comparison and the ring-complex model, respectively.

nodes.title: The Euler and Cartan comparison square
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring, M a module admitting a finite resolution by finite projectives, and h the corresponding admitsFiniteResolution witness. Under c_R, the class of a bounded cochain resolution P•→M[0] (P^i=0 for i>0) is moduleEulerClassOf(R,h)=Σ_i(−1)^i[P^i]. Applying the EXISTING cartanMap sends it to the class of M in ExactK0(finiteModulesExactStructure R). For commutative noetherian R this is precisely π₀ of the scheme Cartan map on Spec R. For flat maps between commutative noetherian rings the resulting Euler/Cartan square commutes with scalar extension on both sides.
hypotheses: No global regularity assumption on R is required for a single M with the stated finite resolution.
The scheme/G-theory and flat-base-change assertions assume commutative noetherian rings. Arbitrary scalar extension on all finitely generated modules is not used as an exact G₀ functor.
proofSteps: Import the finite-resolution equivalence, its inverse-on-classes formula, and moduleEulerClassOf_eq from the pin. Do not construct another resolution class.

The pinned factorisation cartanMap = fromFiniteProjectiveResolution ∘ moduleResolutionEquiv sends the inverse image of [M] to [M]; this proves the native identity without assuming every finite module has a finite resolution.
K.4/gillet-waldhausen and the alternating truncation filtration identify the perfect-complex class with that resolution class. S.2/cartan-degree-zero-compatibility identifies the affine target map.
Flat scalar extension preserves the resolution and is exact on finite modules; compare generators. More general finite-Tor-dimension derived G-pullback belongs to S.2, not to this elementary square.
acceptance: The one-term projective resolution gives cartanMap([P])=[P].
For ℤ/p, the two terms ℤ in degrees −1 and 0 cancel, so its G₀(ℤ) class is zero.
For k[ε]/ε², the map in projective-rank/simple-length bases is ×2; no inverse or finite projective resolution of its residue field is inferred.

sources.locator: II Theorem 9.2.2 and proof, book pp.162–163 (PDF pp.170–171); II.9.7.5, book p.169 (PDF p.177)
sources.match: The class of a bounded projective complex is the alternating class of its terms.

sources.locator: CartanMap.lean: moduleEulerClassOf_eq, moduleResolutionEquiv_symm_of, fromFiniteProjectiveResolution_of and cartanMap_apply (lines358–409)
sources.match: These existing formulas give the comparison with the same Cartan map, including its exact structures.

nodes.title: Localisation, support and rank–Pic coordinates
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A and multiplicative set S, the degree-zero support-forgetful and restriction maps form K₀(A on S)→RingK0(A)→RingK0(S⁻¹A), exact at the middle. A supported strictly perfect cochain complex maps to its alternating class and then to zero; [P] restricts to [S⁻¹P]. If A is Dedekind, under the existing rank–Pic isomorphisms restriction is (r,L)↦(r,S⁻¹L) for S not containing zero; the rank–Pic coordinates of a supported Euler class are (Σ(−1)^i rk P^i, ⊗_i det(P^i)^{(−1)^i}). The affine scheme diagram and the Cartan diagram for this flat localisation commute.
hypotheses: For a single open-support localisation sequence on schemes require a qcqs open complement; arbitrary S uses the ring localisation model/filtered limit, not an unproved quasi-compactness assertion for Spec S⁻¹A→Spec A.
The rank–Pic equivalence is imported only in its Dedekind hypotheses. If 0∈S the target ring is zero and there is no target rank copy of ℤ.
proofSteps: Import the support category and the exact degree-zero sequence. Compare restriction on projectives using affine-comparison-diagram; use the finite-complex Euler formula for the forgetful arrow.
For Dedekind A apply Z.4/k0-localization to the rank and determinant maps. Extension of invertible modules respects tensor and dual, hence the indicated Pic map.

Flatness of localisation gives resolution-euler-cartan-square. Compare the determinant formula term by term with rank-pic-determinant-square. Exactness at K₀(A) never adds an unsupported surjectivity assertion on K₀(S⁻¹A).
acceptance: For A=ℤ and S=ℤ\{0}, restriction is identity on ℤ and the support-forgetful map is zero.
For A=F×F and S generated by (1,0), restriction (a,b)↦a kills [0×F].
For I=(2,1+√−5) in ℤ[√−5], the resolution I→A in degrees −1,0 forgets to [A]−[I], with determinant I⁻¹. It dies over the fraction field, although its global class is nonzero.

sources.match: Supported perfect complexes forget by Euler class; localisation is exact at the middle and rank/determinant are additive invariants.

nodes.title: Components of the graded determinant agree with Euler rank and Picard class
nodes.statement: For qcqs X, the map π₀Det_X:π₀K(Perf X)→π₀Pic^ℤ(X)=H⁰(X,ℤ)⊕Pic(X) has, on a strictly perfect cochain representative P•, value (Σ_i(−1)^i rk P^i, ⊗_i det P^i to exponent (−1)^i). Precomposition with K₀(Vect X)→π₀K(Perf X) is exactly the existing rank–determinant map of Z.5; when X has the resolution property this is a comparison through an isomorphism. This equality is natural for derived pullback. Composing only the component-group map with Pic projection gives the ordinary determinant homomorphism, without a symmetric-monoidal forget-grade factorisation.
hypotheses: Rank is a locally constant integer function. Do not replace H⁰(X,ℤ) by ℤ unless X is nonempty and connected.
A global term formula is used only when a global bounded vector-bundle representative is given; general perfect objects use descent of the local formulas.
Pic^ℤ uses the symmetry (−1)^{fg} times the line-bundle flip, with line first and grade second when writing a Picard object (L,f).
proofSteps: Use old bounded-complex-det and graded-det-pi-zero, identifying their projective and affine normalisations by affine-comparison-diagram. The tensor product in Pic^ℤ is the image of direct sum in K, not the K-ring product.
On a bundle E[0] the formula is (rk E,det E), so generator extensionality identifies it with Z.5’s map. Shift introduces the additive inverse and line dual; triangle additivity gives the Euler sum.
Pullback preserves the imported finite-locally-free determinant and the coherent spectrum map. The sign survives passage to automorphisms; forgetting it is valid only after taking components.
acceptance: On F×F, [F×0] has grade (1,0), not an integer constant.
O_X[1] has object (O_X,−1), while the zero complex has (O_X,0).
Over a field of characteristic ≠2, interchanging two rank-one summands acts as −1 on their determinant line. An unsigned Picard target fails this check.
On ℙ¹, z=[O]−[O(−1)] has components (0,O(1)); its rank is zero but its determinant is nontrivial.

sources.locator: §5, Construction5.1 and Proposition5.3, pp.18–19; §12, Example12.2(iii) and Corollary12.17, pp.54–55,59
sources.match: The signed graded determinant preserves direct sums and has the stated affine/scheme normalisation.
Its rank and determinant maps are the component invariants compared here.

nodes.title: Functorial comparison of the two projective-line coordinate systems
nodes.statement: Use the existing projective-bundle coordinates x=a[O]+b[O(−1)] on K₀(ℙ¹_F), and the existing rank–determinant coordinates (r,d). For every field extension F→E, base change is the identity on BOTH copies of ℤ² and conjugates the comparison (a,b)↦(a+b,−b). Under it proper pushforward π_* is (a,b)↦a=(r,d)↦r+d and either standard section pullback σ* is (a,b)↦a+b=(r,d)↦r. These assertions use the SAME π₀K comparison and Cartan equivalence as the affine tests. The ring product in rank–degree coordinates is (r,d)(s,e)=(rs,re+sd).
hypotheses: F and E are fields, ℙ¹ has O(−1) as its projective-bundle generator. Pushforward is the existing proper perfect pushforward.
The coordinate statements concern K₀, not a direct-sum splitting of graded Picard spectra or an origin-free genus-one formula.
proofSteps: Import S.5/projective-line-k-theory and the three existing Z.6 projective-line nodes, rather than reproving the projective bundle theorem or Pic(ℙ¹).
Evaluate pullback of O and O(−1) under the field extension, preserving these two ordered generators. Their coordinate columns prove both identities and the commuting base-change diagram.
Use π_*O=1, π_*O(−1)=0 and σ*O=σ*O(−1)=1 from S.5. Substitution gives π_*=r+d and σ*=r. The Z.5 ring formula transports the product.
acceptance: O(m) has (a,b)=(m+1,−m), (r,d)=(1,m), including m=−2 where π_* is −1.
The rational skyscraper z has (1,−1) and (0,1); π_*z=1, σ*z=0 in K₀, and z²=0. Section pullback here is DERIVED; naive restriction of the skyscraper at the section would give the wrong answer.
The coordinate matrix [[1,1],[0,−1]] squares to identity. Swapping the O(1)/O(−1) convention changes the signs and fails the preceding tests.

sources.locator: II Theorem8.5 and Corollary8.6, book p.149 (PDF p.157); V Theorem1.5.4, book p.371 (PDF p.379)
sources.match: These give the ordered two-generator basis and its twisting relation; the functorial coordinate comparison is obtained by applying the imported pullbacks and pushforward.

nodes.title: Affine descent comparison for the scheme determinant
nodes.statement: The ordinary scheme determinant already specified in scheme-spectrum-det is the Zariski descent of the affine signed determinant with its scalar-extension comparison. Its affine restriction comparison is compatible with identity/composition of pullbacks, the zero object, shifts, and additivity paths for enhanced cofiber sequences. Consequently its component map is the one in rank-pic-determinant-square. A change of affine presentation gives equivalent determinant data through the descent comparison, not merely an equality of Picard classes.
hypotheses: X is qcqs; no regularity or resolution property is needed for Det on Perf(X).

Use enhanced Perf and mapping spaces (or Picard-groupoid pseudofunctors with monoidal natural isomorphisms after truncation). A bare triangulated category does not supply canonical triangle/octahedral comparison data.
The coherent generic truncation/descent and filtered additivity interfaces are explicit supplier requests; no new generic spectra theory is owned here.
proofSteps: Import the affine map and its Zariski-sheafified normalisation from Z.3. Identify scalar-extension restrictions by affine-comparison-diagram and the finite-locally-free pullback/determinant operations owned by AlgebraicVectorBundles L0A–L0C.

Pic^ℤ is a Zariski stack; the affine normalisations and their overlap isomorphisms descend to a map K(Perf X)→Pic^ℤ(X), as in BS17 Prop5.3. This only needs descent for maps INTO the stack; no claim that an arbitrary connective K presheaf is itself hypercomplete is required.
Use K.4’s requested coherent additivity to transport enhanced triangles and filtrations, retaining the extension paths. Apply π₀ to recover the earlier Euler comparison.
acceptance: On a singular affine scheme the map still exists, without identifying Vect K and Perf K on all schemes.
On the doubled affine plane the Perf determinant exists; the failed Vect→Perf equivalence must not be used to define it.
A swap of two degree-zero lines has sign −1 in characteristic ≠2; neither descent nor passing to a new representative erases that automorphism.

sources.locator: §5 Proposition5.3 and its proof, pp.18–19; §12 Corollary12.17 and Proposition12.18, p.59
sources.match: The scheme map is obtained from the affine determinant and Zariski descent, with a groupoid/spectrum-valued target.

nodes.title: The sheafified comparison defining the supported Witt determinant
nodes.statement: On the site of perfect qcqs F_p-schemes let A=τ≤1K(Perf−), B=τ≤1K(W(−) on −), P=Pic^ℤ, and a_v denote sheafification in 1-truncated connective spectra/Picard groupoids. The supplier gives a_vα:a_vA≃a_vB, and ordinary determinant gives a_vA≃P. Define e:a_vB≃P as their composite using the inverse of a_vα. The EXISTING supported determinant is K(W(−) on −)→B→a_vB→e P. Restriction along α identifies it with Det, including the extension homotopy. Precomposition along α induces an equivalence of natural mapping spaces into P; its homotopy fibre over the specified ordinary Det is contractible. This is uniqueness of NATURAL extensions with the extension homotopy.
hypotheses: p is prime, W denotes p-typical Witt vectors, and the support input is the S.3 enhanced formal-Witt category.
P is a v-stack; use the universal properties of τ≤1 and sheafification at the level of mapping groupoids/spaces, requested from the indicated suppliers.
There is no assertion that α_X is an equivalence for every X, nor that all maps out of the supported K-spectrum at a fixed X form a contractible space.
proofSteps: Replace the old broad support/site edges by S.3/witt-supported-perfect-complexes, S.3/witt-special-fibre-k-map, S.4/perfect-scheme-h-and-v-sites and S.4/witt-k-one-truncation-sheafification. Keep W(X) formal; on affines its model is Spec W(R) with p support.
Use Z.3/graded-pic-v-descent and ordinary Det normalisation. The maps A→P and α become equivalences after sheafification; their inverse/composite gives e.

For a 1-truncated sheaf P, natural maps from supported K to P factor through B and then a_vB. Precomposition by a_vα is an equivalence; a fibre of an equivalence over a specified point is contractible. This proves the extension property and its coherent uniqueness together.

The h-local proof of the α comparison uses regular finite-type perfections and alterations, so the smooth case suffices. The broader arbitrary regular Cor5.6 claim remains subject to the supplier’s Popescu/continuity gap; do not reproduce its faulty blanket smooth-lift step.
acceptance: Over a perfect field k, the residue module α(k) maps to (k,1).
W(k)/p² has supported determinant grade2 even though its ordinary W(k)-projective resolution has virtual W(k)-rank0. The two determinant targets differ.
The zero object has (O,0). W(k)[0] is not a supported input when k is a nonzero field.
The mapping-space argument retains the chosen extension homotopy; equality on π₀ is insufficient to prove uniqueness.

sources.locator: §5 Theorem5.7 and proof, pp.19–20; Proposition12.18, p.59
sources.match: The proof sheafifies the one-truncations and determines the supported extension with its natural homotopy; it does not give objectwise equivalence for all perfect schemes.

nodes.title: Filtration and base-change comparisons for supported determinants
nodes.statement: For a finite enhanced filtration 0=C₀→⋯→C_n=C in Perf(W(X) on X), supplied identifications cofib(C_{j−1}→C_j)≃α_X(D_j) give Det~(C)≃⊗_{j=1}^n Det(D_j), ordered by increasing filtration index. These isomorphisms commute with perfect-scheme derived pullback and with specified refinement diagrams through the K-theory additivity paths. In particular, for perfect k, a finite-length W(k)-module Q, and perfect qcqs k-scheme X, a finite filtration of Q_X by finite projective O_X-graded pieces has product determinant line pulled back from the k-line underlying Det~(Q). It is trivializable, with locally constant grade length_{W(k)}Q. No canonical basis or individual triviality of every graded determinant is asserted.
hypotheses: The filtration includes actual enhanced maps, cofiber identifications and refinement comparisons; a list of equal component classes is insufficient.

In the constant-module clause k is a nonzero perfect field, X is a perfect k-scheme, Q_X is the derived Witt base change, agreeing with the ordinary tensor module here; W(O_X) is flat over the DVR W(k) on affines.
For arbitrary filtrations, comparison follows the specified paths. Contractible uniqueness of the global natural extension is not a claim that every automorphism of each determinant line is trivial.
proofSteps: Use the requested coherent Waldhausen additivity to obtain the path [C]=Σ[α(D_j)] in supported K, then apply the SAME Det~ of witt-determinant-sheafification-square and its specified extension homotopy.
Naturality of additivity and of Det~ gives the base-change square. The octahedral/refinement coherence is imported from K.4, not inferred from the triangulated axioms alone.

For constant Q, naturality identifies Det~(Q_X) with pullback of Det~(Q). Every line over k has a basis, hence its pullback is trivializable. A composition series of Q has length ℓ and k-graded pieces, giving grade ℓ. Any other specified filtration gives the same determinant via additivity.
acceptance: Q=0 gives the empty tensor product and grade0.
Q=k gives a trivializable line with grade1; Q=W(k)/p² gives grade2, not the graded tensor unit.
A nontrivial automorphism u∈k× acts on the residue-line determinant; trivializable does not mean canonically trivialized.
Refining the length-two p-adic filtration preserves its ordered determinant comparison and commutes with base change to any perfect k-scheme.

sources.locator: §5 Theorem5.7, pp.19–20; Lemma6.11 and its K-theoretic proof, pp.24–25
sources.match: The constant Witt-torsion determinant is a pullback of a field line; coherent additivity converts a filtration to its product determinant without selecting a basis.

coverage.note: All original degree-zero comparison/test targets and the BS17 scheme/Witt determinant extension are accounted for by the inherited targetDisposition and the eight refinement nodes. The new packet imports every earlier target by its existing ID; it does not replace or duplicate the accepted packet. Each imported construction has an API/test audit in the reader.
remaining: Supply enriched Picard/truncation/sheafification mapping interfaces and coherent K-theory filtration additivity at the owners named in requests.
The arbitrary-regular Cor5.6 target retains the supplier’s Popescu/supported-continuity gap; the smooth finite-type case suffices for the determinant descent route.
Formalise the planned comparison maps when their actual carriers exist; the native Lean companion records only signatures available at the pins.

gaps.title: Enriched natural mapping and sheafification interface
gaps.detail: The accepted H.5 Picard comparison is stated only at homotopy-theory/2-category level and has an explicit unread comparison gap. A homotopy-category equivalence alone does not supply the mapping-groupoid universal properties used to prove contractibility of natural determinant extensions. Request the precise 1-truncated enriched interface, including sheafification into Picard stacks; S.4’s one-truncation equivalence by itself does not specify it.

gaps.title: Coherent finite-filtration additivity interface
gaps.detail: Ordinary triangle relations in TriangulatedK0 and the homotopy-category Waldhausen additivity statement do not fix natural determinant isomorphisms and refinement diagrams. The generic owner must supply enhanced cofiber-additivity paths, naturality, unit and octahedral/refinement coherence. The read source asserts the determinant theorem, but these formal supplier interfaces remain open.

gaps.title: Inherited arbitrary-regular Witt comparison gap
gaps.detail: S.3/witt-regular-perfection-devissage explicitly leaves Popescu approximation and continuity of the supported Witt comparison for arbitrary regular noetherian F_p-algebras open. Import its corrected contract; do not justify it by a smooth Frobenius lift for arbitrary R₀. This is needed for the inherited broader Cor5.6 target, while the smooth alteration-basis proof of the supported determinant avoids that broader case.

requests.need: Extend the Picard/1-truncated connective spectrum comparison to mapping groupoids (symmetric monoidal functors and monoidal natural isomorphisms), compatible with functor-category limits and τ≤1’s universal property. Identify the homotopy fibre of precomposition by an equivalence over a specified map with a contractible space.

Expose the Picard-stack/1-truncated spectrum sheafification universal property: natural maps B→P for a v-stack P are equivalent as mapping groupoids to maps a_v B→P, with pullback, units and extension homotopies retained. This is an interface extension to the existing comparison, not a second support/descent theorem.

Expose enhanced cofiber-sequence additivity paths in K, naturality under exact functors and maps of filtrations, empty-filtration/unit compatibility, and common-refinement/octahedral coherence. Do not replace them by equalities only on π₀ or arbitrary choices of cones.

Complete the already recorded Popescu plus supported-Witt/perfection continuity bridge for arbitrary regular noetherian R₀; keep the smooth finite-type lift proof distinct. This request continues the existing E31 correction and records no new source finding.

regressionTests.nonprincipalIdeal: The ideal I=(2,1+s) in Z[s]/(s²+5) has quotient F₂; its norm-two nonprincipality and I²=(2) calculation are worked in the reader. Since its class has order two, the P¹ and order-four elliptic tests additionally detect inversion signs.
regressionTests.ellipticFiniteEnumeration: For y²=x³−x over F₅ enumerate all eight points and the group law. Q=(2,1) has double (0,0) and order4; three nonzero points have order2. E(F₅) is Z/4×Z/2. Imported E.2 identifies the degree-zero Picard test class with Q.
regressionTests.projectiveLine: The inverse coordinate matrix, all integer twists, the tensor-product formula, proper pushforward and derived section-pullback are compared, including z²=0 and O(−2).
